events.title: The Spanish Armada Is Sighted in the English Channel
events.description: English lookouts spotted the great Spanish fleet off the coast of Cornwall. The sighting set in motion the running sea battles that followed in the days after. Beacons and messengers carried the alarm across England.
events.significance: The failure of the Armada to invade England became a turning point in European naval power and a lasting symbol of English resilience.

events.title: Five Women Hanged in the Salem Witch Trials
events.description: Five women were executed by hanging in Salem, Massachusetts, after being convicted of witchcraft. They were Sarah Good, Elizabeth Howe, Susannah Martin, Rebecca Nurse and Sarah Wildes. The hysteria gripping the colony had by then led to dozens of accusations.
events.significance: The Salem trials have become a enduring cautionary tale about mass hysteria, flawed legal process, and the danger of persecution.

events.title: Seneca Falls Convention Opens
events.description: A two-day women's rights convention began in Seneca Falls, New York. It was organized by activists including Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott. Attendees debated and later adopted a Declaration of Sentiments calling for equality.
events.significance: The convention is widely regarded as the starting point of the organized women's suffrage movement in the United States.

events.title: Maurice Garin Wins the First Tour de France
events.description: French cyclist Maurice Garin crossed the finish line to win the inaugural Tour de France. The race had been created to boost newspaper sales. Riders faced huge distances on rough roads.
events.significance: The race grew into the world's most famous cycling event and a cornerstone of the sport.
